meta.purpose: Every irregularity, unverified value, and compliance risk found while building this site. Each flag is published on the 'Flagged for Review' page with its source links.

flags.title: Prices on this site were captured manually, which the Program Policies do not permit
flags.detail: Associates Program Policies, Participation Requirements section 2(b) states: 'Product prices and availability may vary from time to time. Because prices for and availability of Products that you have listed on your Site may change, your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements regarding use of Creators API or PA API in the License.' Every price on this site was read by hand from an Amazon search results page. Neither condition (a) nor (b) is met.
flags.action_required: Before the site goes live, replace every static price with an Amazon-served widget, or with data pulled through Creators API / PA API, or delete the price columns entirely. Do not publish the current hand-captured prices on a live monetised page.

flags.title: Limited-time promotion badges are displayed and must be removed the moment the promotion ends
flags.detail: All three products carried a live promotion badge at capture time: B0CDY277D3 'Limited time deal', B08DKYBTPH 'Limited time deal', B09B7SB46R 'Early Black Friday Deal'. Participation Requirements section 2(b) states: 'You must remove from your Site any links and related references to limited time promotions as soon as that promotion on the relevant Amazon Site ends.'
flags.action_required: Do not publish the deal badges on a live page unless the page is updated at least daily from a live feed. Safest option: remove the badge column before launch.

flags.title: Best Sellers Rank could not be verified for any of the three products
flags.detail: Amazon product detail pages (/dp/ASIN, /gp/aw/d/ASIN, and the canonical slug URLs) returned a 'shuffle' landing variant with no extractable product-detail block in this session, and /product-reviews/ASIN redirected to an Amazon sign-in wall. Best Sellers Rank is only published on the product detail page, so it could not be read from any official page. The field is left blank on this site.
flags.action_required: Read BSR from the live product detail page, or from PA-API GetItems (Offers/BestSellersRank) once credentials exist. Until then it stays blank.

flags.title: Rating counts are Amazon's rounded display values, not exact counts
flags.detail: Amazon search results render rating counts as '4.8K', '18.3K' and '16.8K'. The exact review counts are only available on the review pages, which require sign-in. The rounded values are marked as rounded everywhere they appear on this site, and the exact-count column is deliberately left blank.
flags.action_required: Populate exact counts from PA-API or by reading the signed-in review page. Do not treat 4.8K / 18.3K / 16.8K as exact.

flags.title: None of the supplied links contains an Amazon Associates tag, so no commission can accrue
flags.detail: Participation Requirements section 2(b) requires that 'you must include your Associates ID or tag (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site.' The three supplied short links and the canonical URLs they resolve to contain no tag parameter. As supplied they are plain product links, not Special Links.
flags.action_required: Add an approved Associates tag to every outbound link before launch. The Link Builder page on this site generates the tagged URL once a tag is supplied. Note that the tag must be inserted by the associate; this project cannot know it.

flags.title: Operator is located in Oslo, Norway; the applicable regional Associates program is unconfirmed
flags.detail: The Associates Central country selector lists United States, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Japan, Canada, Italy, Spain, India, Brazil, Mexico, Australia, United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Netherlands, Saudi Arabia, Sweden, Poland, Belgium, Ireland, Turkey and Egypt. Norway is not among them. All product data captured here is from Amazon.com (US). Which regional program the operator should join, and therefore which commission schedule and tax schedule applies, has not been determined. Participation Requirements section 3 also puts GDPR and the ePrivacy Directive (2002/58/EC) in scope for EU/EEA operators, which affects the cookie and tracking consent design on the site.
flags.action_required: Decide the target marketplace (US vs. a European store) before data collection is repeated, and build a consent layer that satisfies GDPR / ePrivacy if EU/EEA visitors are targeted.

flags.title: The 'link.amazon' short-link host is not documented on any official Amazon page we could find
flags.detail: All three supplied links use the host link.amazon. Each was fetched and each returned an official Amazon.com product page (B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH), so the redirects are genuine and the resolved ASINs are confirmed. However no official Amazon page documenting link.amazon as an Amazon-owned shortener was located in this session. The resolution is treated as observed behaviour, not as documented policy.
flags.action_required: Confirm the provenance of these short links with whoever supplied them, and prefer canonical /dp/ASIN URLs on published pages so the destination is visible to visitors.

flags.title: Amazon's 'bought in past month' signal may not be republished verbatim
flags.detail: Amazon displayed '1K+ bought in past month', '4K+ bought in past month' and '3K+ bought in past month'. This is Amazon-rendered Program Content adjacent to the product listing. Content-on-your-Site rule 6(a) states 'You will not add to, delete from, or otherwise alter any Program Content in any way.' The signal is reproduced verbatim here, but it is volatile Amazon content and its reuse should be cleared before publication.
flags.action_required: Prefer Amazon-served widgets for this signal, or drop the column before launch.

flags.title: The applicable commission rate for these ASINs could be Kitchen (4.50%) or Home (3.00%)
flags.detail: The Associates Standard Commission Income Statement lists 'Kitchen' at 4.50% and 'Home' at 3.00% as separate categories. All three products sit in the Amazon department 'Home & Kitchen' and in the browse path Home & Kitchen > Kitchen & Dining > Small Appliances > Fryers > Air Fryers. Amazon assigns the commission category internally per ASIN and does not publish that assignment, so the applicable rate cannot be confirmed from an official source without PA-API/Associates Central data.
flags.action_required: Confirm the rate per ASIN in Associates Central reports or via PA-API before relying on the revenue model. This site shows 4.50% as the primary case and 3.00% as the downside case, and labels both as illustrative.

flags.title: Product specifications beyond the title are unverified
flags.detail: Wattage, model number, dimensions, warranty and country of origin are not exposed on any official page reachable in this session. Only the capacity stated inside the official product title (6 Quart / 26 QT / 8 Qt) is verified. All other specification cells are left blank.
flags.action_required: Pull specifications from PA-API GetItems (ItemInfo) once credentials exist, or copy them verbatim from the Amazon detail page.

flags.title: The repository contained no prior work to review
flags.detail: At the start of this session the repository had exactly one commit (ed1a796 'Initial commit') and one file, README.md, whose entire content is '# Zone3'. There were no existing findings, tables, datasets or code to verify line by line, no other branches, and no other sessions active in COORDINATION.md.
flags.action_required: None. Recorded for completeness of the repo review.

flags.title: The 180-day / three-sale rule and the exact disclosure sentence were read from the official Associates FAQ, not from the Operating Agreement body
flags.detail: The Amazon Associates FAQ page at amazon.com/b?node=51812349011 states: 'Once you've applied, you have 180 days to refer a sale through one of your Associates links. Once you have referred three qualifying sales, we'll evaluate your application within a day or two' and 'the Operating Agreement requires that the following statement clearly and conspicuously appears on your Site: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."' The FAQ page is a 29-chunk document and the Policies section containing that sentence was not individually retrieved chunk-by-chunk in this session; the wording was read from the retrieved index of that official page body. The Operating Agreement chunks that were fully retrieved (sections 1-3 and 7-12) do not contain the sentence.
flags.action_required: Before publication, open the Operating Agreement and copy the exact current disclosure sentence verbatim. The site currently renders the FAQ wording and labels it as such.

flags.title: Participation Requirements demand original content that is not yet written
flags.detail: Participation Requirements section 1 states: 'Your Site(s) must contain original content and be publicly available via the website address provided in the application. Original content utilizing third-party materials must contain significant commentary, analysis, or transformation to any materials you include.' This site is currently a data dashboard of Amazon-supplied facts. It does not yet contain the product articles, comparisons or buying guides the brief asks for.
flags.action_required: Write original buying guides and comparison articles before applying to the program. A table of Amazon data alone is unlikely to pass the suitability review.

flags.title: No click or conversion data exists yet; all tracking surfaces show 'no data'
flags.detail: The brief asks the platform to track clicks and conversions and to optimise campaigns. No Associates account, no tag and no traffic exist yet, so there is no real click or conversion data. Rather than populate the dashboard with placeholder numbers, every analytics figure on this site is rendered as 'no data yet - pre-launch'. Fabricated conversion metrics would be indistinguishable from real ones in a table and are therefore not produced.
flags.action_required: Wire the outbound-click logger to a real backend, then populate these surfaces from real data.

flags.title: All commercial values on this site are a snapshot taken on 2026-11-13 and go stale immediately
flags.detail: Prices, deal badges, ratings, rating counts, 'bought in past month' signals and best-seller positions all change continuously on Amazon. The snapshot timestamps are shown next to every volatile value so a reviewer can tell how old it is. Nothing here should be treated as current without re-checking the linked official page.
flags.action_required: Re-run the collector before any decision is made on these numbers, or move to a live API feed.

flags.title: Training AI models on Amazon Program Content or Special Links needs Amazon's express prior written approval
flags.detail: Associates Program Policies, Participation Requirements section 5 (Distribution of Special Links Through Software and Devices) states: 'You will not, without our express prior written approval, use, or allow any third party to use, any Special Links or Program Content to develop machine learning models or related technology.' The brief asks for an AI-powered platform that automates research and generates content. Any part of that platform which trains, fine-tunes or evaluates a model on Amazon-sourced product data, images, reviews or link data falls inside this restriction unless Amazon has approved it in writing. Using a general-purpose AI model to write or edit copy is a different activity from training a model on Program Content, but the boundary between the two is a decision for a reviewer, not for an automated build.
flags.action_required: Before any training or fine-tuning on Amazon-sourced data, obtain Amazon's express prior written approval, or restrict the AI layer to operating on data you collected lawfully outside the Associates Program. Keep a written record of whichever path is chosen.

flags.title: Automated collection and bot traffic carry specific restrictions under the Program Policies
flags.detail: Associates Program Policies, Commission Income Statement section 5 states that Associates' tags 'should only be used to benefit from Amazon Associates commissions' and that Amazon may withhold commissions or terminate participation if it detects an attempt 'to claim commissions from both Amazon Associates and another program using the same traffic (for example, by manipulating or combining attribution links)'. The Bonus Event provisions separately disqualify activity generated by 'bots or automated software'. Taken together, an automation platform that drives or simulates traffic through its own Special Links, or that double-attributes the same traffic to two programs, risks termination. Automated collection of publicly visible Amazon pages is also governed by Amazon's own Conditions of Use, which were not retrieved in this session.
flags.action_required: Restrict automation to back-office work: reading your own Associates reports, updating your own pages, and drafting content for human review. Do not let automated processes click, visit or transact through your own Special Links. Retrieve and review Amazon's Conditions of Use before building any collector that runs unattended.

flags.title: No trend or seasonality analysis was possible from official sources
flags.detail: The brief asks the platform to identify trending products. Trend requires a time series, and a time series requires repeated captures over weeks or months. This session produced a single snapshot. Amazon's Best Sellers pages state their own basis, 'Our most popular products based on sales. Updated frequently', and give the current ranking only, with no historical series. Publishing a trend line from one data point would be fabrication.
flags.action_required: Run the collector on a fixed schedule for at least eight to twelve weeks before any trend claim is made. The Automation Architecture page specifies the collector contract needed to build that series.

flags.title: The site ships with noindex/nofollow until the blockers above are cleared
flags.detail: Every page carries <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">. This is deliberate. The site displays hand-captured prices (FLAG-01), live promotion badges (FLAG-02) and Amazon's own 'bought in past month' signal (FLAG-08), and it has no Associates tag (FLAG-05). Publicly indexing a page set in that state would put policy-violating content into search results, and an affiliate site with no working tag earns nothing from the traffic anyway.
flags.action_required: Remove the robots meta tag from the page template only after FLAG-01, FLAG-02, FLAG-05 and FLAG-13 are closed. Removing it earlier exposes policy-violating content to search engines; leaving it on a finished site means the site cannot be found.
